Home

About Us

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Technology for the Modern Forex Brokerage

We're a forex technology company that builds and looks after the systems brokerages run on. Trading platforms, servers, liquidity links, CRMs, payment and verification integrations, apps and the APIs that hold them together.

Who We Are

Our team is made up of platform engineers, integration developers, infrastructure specialists and people who've spent years inside brokerage operations. That last part matters. We understand why a withdrawal queue needs certain checks, why a symbol mapping error can cost real money, and why a dealing desk gets twitchy when a price feed goes quiet.

We started because we kept seeing the same problem. Brokers bought a platform from one company, a CRM from another, hosting from a third and liquidity connectivity from a fourth. When something broke, every vendor blamed someone else. We set out to be the team that takes responsibility for how the whole stack fits together.

HOW WE WORK

Understand

Connect

Support

Integrated technology workflow

Our Expertise

Our work spans the full technology layer of a brokerage:

* MT5 and MT4 deployment, configuration and maintenance

* White label and grey label platform setups

* Trading server hosting, monitoring and disaster recovery

* Liquidity connectivity through bridges, gateways and FIX

* Forex CRM, client portals and back office tooling

* KYC, AML screening and payment provider integrations

* Branded mobile and web trading experiences

* Prop firm evaluation systems and APIs

Some clients use us for one of these. Others hand us the entire stack. Either way, the depth of knowledge behind each piece is the same.

What We Deliver

Our work falls into three broad areas.

Solutions

For businesses setting up or running a brokerage. MT5 and MT4 white and grey label setups, turnkey launches, hosting and liquidity connectivity.

Products

Specific tools brokers plug into their operations. CRM, broker websites, mobile and web trading apps, manager APIs, PAMM and MAM, prop firm systems and payment integrations.

Technology

The infrastructure underneath. Servers, bridges, FIX connectivity, verification and payment integrations, security, monitoring and backups.

How We Work

Every project follows the same four stages. We start with a consultation to understand your business properly. We then design the solution and agree it with you in writing. Next comes integration, where everything is built, connected and tested thoroughly. Finally, we launch with you and stay on to support what we've built.

Clear stages, clear deliverables and no work you haven't approved.

Support That Doesn't Disappear

Plenty of technology providers are very attentive until the invoice is paid. We see launch as the start of the relationship, not the end.

After go-live, our engineers handle monitoring, updates, configuration changes and problem-solving for the environments we've built. Because we set them up, we already know how they work, which means faster answers when something needs fixing.

Home

Solutions

Brokerage Setup

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Forex Brokerage Setup & Launch Technology

A forex brokerage setup is a lot more than buying a platform and switching it on. Servers need hosting and securing. Liquidity has to be connected and tested. And clients need a way to sign up, get verified and fund an a

Who This Is For

Mostly, people at the very start. Or close to it.

That could be a founder who wants to start a forex brokerage and has nothing technical in place yet. It could be an introducing broker with a loyal client base, ready to run things under their own name. Sometimes it's a group opening a second entity for a new region, or a fintech business stepping into trading services for the first time.

You don't have to show up with everything figured out. A lot of our clients arrive with a business model, a target market and a rough idea of timing. We help fill in the rest.

Already running a brokerage and just need parts of it fixed or replaced? Our maintenance, hosting and integration services will probably suit you better.

BROKERAGE LAUNCH

Planning

Trading platform

Connected operations

Integrated technology workflow

What Goes Into a Technology-Led Launch

Every project gets scoped around your model, so no two look identical. That said, most launches cover the same core layers.

Choosing and Configuring the Platform

First question: full MT5 deployment or white label? A white label usually costs less and gets you live sooner. A full deployment gives you more control. We'll help you weigh it up against your budget and where you want to be in two or three years.

Once that's decided, we configure the platform properly. Trading groups, account types, symbol specs, leverage and margin rules, and manager access for your dealing and support teams.

Servers and Infrastructure

Your platform needs somewhere to live. We set up hosting in a region that makes sense for your clients and your liquidity, lock down access, schedule backups and get monitoring running before launch day. A backup server and a recovery plan are built in from the start, because adding them later is always harder.

Connecting Liquidity

Depending on what your providers support and how you plan to execute, we'll connect through a bridge, an MT5 gateway or a direct FIX connection. Symbols get mapped. Price feeds get checked. Orders route the way your risk policy says they should.

CRM, KYC and Payments

This is the bit your clients actually notice. Registration, identity checks, account creation, deposits and withdrawals all have to work together, and they all have to talk to the trading platform. We connect your CRM, KYC provider and payment providers so a new client goes from sign-up to a funded account in one smooth flow.

Testing Before Anyone Goes Live

We test everything against real scenarios. Price feeds, order execution, rejects, margin calls, onboarding, deposits, withdrawals, reporting. Finding a problem at this stage costs very little. Finding it after your first hundred clients arrive is a different story.

Support After Launch

The first few weeks are when small issues tend to pop up. We keep a close eye on things during that period, tweak settings as real trading comes in, and then move you onto an ongoing support plan.

How It All Fits Together

Here's the stack in a single line:

Client → Website & Client Portal → CRM, KYC & Payments → MT5 Trading Server → Bridge / Gateway / FIX → Liquidity Providers → Reporting & Back Office

A client signs up on your website. The CRM records them, the KYC provider verifies them, the payment provider handles their deposit. Their trading account opens on MT5. When they trade, orders travel through your connectivity layer to liquidity, and the results flow back into your reports.

If one link is set up badly, everything downstream feels it. So we build and test the whole chain as one system.

Key Capabilities

* MT5 server deployment, white label configuration and manager setup

* Hosting across regions, with security hardening, monitoring and backups

* Bridge, gateway and FIX connectivity, including symbol mapping and price-feed checks

* Primary and backup liquidity routes where needed

* CRM integration for leads, client records, trading accounts and IB tracking

* KYC integration with approval and rejection workflows plus audit trails

* Payment provider integration for deposits and withdrawals, including webhooks and reconciliation

* Structured testing with documented test cases and sign-off

* Monitoring after launch and a handover to managed support

A Few Typical Launch Scenarios

Starting From Nothing

A founder has a solid business plan and a licence application underway, but no technology at all. We scope the stack, time the build alongside the regulatory process and have everything tested and waiting for when approval lands.

Turning a Partner Network Into a Brokerage

An introducing broker with a strong client base wants its own brand. We set up an MT5 white label, connect liquidity and build onboarding that makes moving existing clients over as painless as possible.

Opening a Second Entity

An established group wants a separate brokerage for a new market. We design infrastructure that reuses what already works, while keeping the new entity's servers, data and client flows properly apart.

Home

Products

Forex CRM

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Forex CRM Software for Brokers

Ask any brokerage operations manager where the day disappears, and you'll hear the same answers. Chasing missing ID documents. Matching deposits to the right client. Working out which introducer referred whom. Creating trading accounts by hand. Pulling numbers together for the weekly meeting.

What Is a Forex CRM?

General sales CRMs were designed for tracking deals and phone calls. They have no idea what a margin account is, how a withdrawal request should be checked, or why an introducing broker expects a rebate on every lot traded.

A CRM built for brokers handles all of that. It manages prospects and sales activity, yes, but it also runs onboarding, identity checks, funding, trading account creation, partner commissions and reporting. Many brokers think of it as their back office and their client portal rolled together, since clients log in to it too, to upload documents, deposit money and open new accounts.

CONNECTED CLIENT LIFECYCLE

Onboarding

CRM & KYC

MT5 accounts

Integrated technology workflow

Who Uses It

* Newly launched brokers who need a client lifecycle in place before the first sign-up

* Growing brokerages whose spreadsheets and email threads have stopped scaling

* Firms replacing an older CRM that never integrated properly with their trading server

* Businesses running large introducing broker or affiliate networks

* Brokers with sales teams across several regions and languages

MT5, Payment and KYC Integration

The value of a broker CRM comes almost entirely from how well it links to everything around it.

MT4 and MT5 Connection

The CRM talks to your trading server through manager API access. Accounts are created, balances adjusted after deposits and withdrawals, groups assigned and trading data pulled in for reporting and commission calculation. No retyping between systems.

Payment Provider Integration

Card processors, bank transfer services, local payment methods and crypto gateways can be plugged in. Payment confirmations arrive automatically, so deposits credit without someone checking a bank statement first.

KYC Provider Integration

Automated identity verification, liveness checks and sanctions screening services can be linked, depending on which providers you use and what they support. Results flow straight onto the client profile.

Website and Other Systems

Registration forms on your website feed the CRM directly. Marketing tools, help desk software, telephony and accounting systems can connect through APIs and webhooks where needed.

How the CRM Sits in Your Technology Stack

Client → Broker Website → Forex CRM (KYC, Payments, IB) → MT5 / MT4 Server → Liquidity Bridge → Liquidity Providers

A prospect registers on your website and lands in the CRM. They're verified through the KYC flow, fund through an integrated payment provider and receive a trading account generated on your MT5 or MT4 server. Their trades route out through your bridge to liquidity, while trading data flows back into the CRM to drive reports and partner commissions.

How We Roll It Out

01 Consultation

We map your current process. How leads arrive, how onboarding works today, which payment and verification providers you use, how your partner programme is structured and where things get stuck.

02 Solution Design

We agree on account types, onboarding forms, approval rules, user roles, commission plans and integrations. If you're replacing an existing system, we also plan how client data will move across.

03 Integration

The CRM is configured and branded, connected to your trading server, payment providers and verification services, then tested end to end with realistic client journeys. Your team gets training on the parts they'll use.

04 Launch & Support

We go live, monitor the first weeks closely and stay available for configuration changes, new integrations and technical help as you grow.

item.title: Forex Brokerage Technology FAQs
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Home

FAQ

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Forex Brokerage Technology FAQs

Brokerage technology comes with its own vocabulary, and it's easy to feel lost between gateways, grey labels and webhooks. This forex broker technology FAQ gathers the questions founders, operators and prop firm owners ask us most, answered in plain language.

We build, connect and maintain the systems a brokerage depends on. That covers trading platforms, servers, liquidity connections, CRMs, payment and verification integrations, apps and APIs. The brokerage runs the business, and we make sure the technology underneath it works.

Neither. We're purely a technology company. We don't execute client trades, provide liquidity, hold client money or offer investment advice.

No. Some clients use us for one service, such as hosting or a CRM. Others hand us the whole stack. We're happy to work alongside systems and vendors you already have.

Yes, and plenty of our clients begin exactly there. During the first consultation we'll help you work out what you need, in what order and roughly what it involves.

Licensing is a legal and regulatory matter, so it's outside what we do. We can explain how technology decisions interact with common regulatory expectations, but you'll need qualified advisors in your target jurisdiction for the licence itself.

We support brokerages serving clients in many regions. Where your clients are located does affect choices like hosting location, payment methods and verification providers, which we factor into the design.

Most new brokers now choose MT5. It supports more asset classes, has a more modern architecture and is where the platform developer focuses ongoing work. MT4 still has a loyal user base, so some brokers offer both.

Yes. Many brokers do, either permanently or during a gradual move from one to the other. The two can share liquidity connections and a CRM.

It takes careful planning rather than heavy lifting. Account types, groups, symbols and trading conditions need recreating, integrations need reconnecting and clients need a clear transition path. Phased migrations tend to go smoothest.

No, not unless we state otherwise for a specific arrangement. We work with the platforms as a technology provider.

It's an arrangement where your brokerage runs on MT5 under your own brand, inside an environment operated under an existing platform licence. You get branded access and your own account setup without buying a full server licence yourself.

Mainly cost and speed. A full licence carries a large upfront investment and more technical responsibility. A white label lets you launch sooner and spend less, with the option to move to your own server later.

Usually, yes, within the limits of the arrangement and your liquidity setup. Exactly how much control you get varies by provider, so it's worth confirming before signing.

No. It's a technology arrangement only. Financial licensing is completely separate.

A grey label generally sits more directly under another provider's infrastructure and arrangement, with lower entry costs and less independent control than a white label. Terms vary widely between providers, so definitions aren't always consistent.

In broad terms, a white label gives you more control over branding and configuration, while a grey label trades some of that control for a lighter, cheaper setup. We'll explain exactly what any specific offer includes before you commit.

It can suit smaller or early-stage operations testing the market with limited budget. If you expect fast growth or need detailed control over trading conditions, a white label or full deployment is often a better long-term fit.

Not necessarily. Requirements depend on your jurisdiction, business model and the provider's terms. Take legal advice rather than relying on general claims.

It manages the whole client journey. Lead capture, registration, identity verification, deposits, withdrawals, trading account creation, partner commissions and reporting, usually with a client portal on top.

Yes. It links to MT5 and MT4 through manager API access, so trading accounts are created, balances updated and trading data pulled in automatically.

Yes. Rebate rules are set in the CRM, which then calculates earnings from real trading data, including multi-level partner structures.

In most cases, yes. We map fields between the two systems, run test imports and check records carefully before switching over.

It's software that sits between your trading platform and one or more liquidity providers, passing prices in and orders out. Bridges typically add tools like markups, routing rules and multi-provider pricing.

A gateway is a more direct link between MT5 and an external system. A bridge is separate middleware with extra routing and aggregation features. FIX is the messaging protocol that both commonly use to communicate with providers.

Yes. Multiple providers can be aggregated for pricing or set up as backups for each other.

No. Pricing and fills come from your providers and depend on market conditions. What we make sure of is that the technical link carrying them is accurate and well monitored.

Yes. We host both, along with environments where they run side by side.

Typically near your main liquidity providers, with client access points closer to where your clients trade. Data rules in your markets can also influence the decision.

Your disaster recovery plan kicks in. Depending on your setup, a standby server takes over or the environment is restored from tested backups.

No honest provider can. We reduce risk through monitoring, redundancy, tested backups and a fast response when issues arise.

No. Payment providers process the money. We integrate them with your CRM and trading platform so deposits and withdrawals flow properly.

Usually, yes, as long as they offer usable integration options. We confirm this during the design stage.

No technology can do that alone. It gives your compliance team the workflow and records they need, but compliance obligations stay with your business.

Yes. That includes challenge setup, automated account creation, rule monitoring, risk flags, performance dashboards and payout review workflows.

Yes. We build iOS and Android apps under your brand, connected to your platform, CRM, payments and verification. Publication is subject to app store review.

Yes. We work with manager APIs, payment and verification APIs, webhooks and custom integrations between your systems and third-party tools.

Yes. We provide PAMM and MAM technology for brokers that support money managers, integrated with MT4 or MT5.

It depends on scope, platform choice and how quickly third-party providers complete their onboarding. You'll get a realistic timeline after the solution design stage.

A clear point of contact, an outline of your business model, details of any providers you've chosen and your target timeline. We'll guide you through the rest.

Monitoring, maintenance, configuration changes, updates and technical help, under a support arrangement agreed with you before go-live.

Yes. Your data and your accounts with third-party providers remain yours, and every change we make is documented.

Get in touch. This forex broker technology FAQ grows over time based on what clients ask, so your question may help the next person too.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Home

Solutions

Trading Server Hosting

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Forex Broker Hosting & Trading Server Infrastructure

Your trading server is the one piece of your brokerage that simply can't have a bad day. When it slows down, clients notice. When it goes offline, they start calling, and some of them start looking elsewhere.

Why Reliable Hosting Matters for a Brokerage

Think about a major news release. Thousands of clients log in at once, prices move fast and orders pour in within seconds. That's exactly when weak hosting shows itself. Terminals freeze, history won't load, orders hang.

A regular website can get away with a slow afternoon. A trading server can't. It has to handle sudden spikes, stay connected to liquidity without interruption and keep client data safe the whole time.

General web hosts rarely understand this. They'll sell you a server, but they won't know how MT5 components fit together, why server location matters for liquidity, or what to do when your platform stops responding at 2am during the Asian session.

TRADING INFRASTRUCTURE

Trade servers

Active monitoring

Recovery planning

Integrated technology workflow

Who This Service Is For

* Brokers preparing to launch and setting up their first trading environment

* Brokers on general-purpose hosting who keep hitting slowdowns during busy markets

* Businesses running MT4 and MT5 side by side and wanting both managed in one place

* Brokers with no real disaster recovery plan, or one nobody has ever tested

* Prop firms whose account numbers are growing faster than their current servers can handle

MT5 Hosting

MT5 is built differently. It splits work across several types of servers, typically a main trade server, history servers, access servers for client connections and backup servers ready to step in.

That spread gives MT5 more flexibility and resilience, but it also means more parts to place and manage well. We design your MT5 server hosting around how each component should sit, where access points should go to suit your client base, and how backup servers are kept in sync so failover works when it matters.

What's Included

Server Infrastructure

Properly sized servers for your platform and expected volumes, whether that's cloud, virtual or dedicated hardware. We size for busy market conditions, not quiet Tuesday afternoons, and leave room to grow.

Location Planning

We place your main trading server with your liquidity providers in mind, often in established financial data centre hubs, and put access points closer to where your clients trade from. Data residency rules in your target markets are taken into account too.

Monitoring

Server resources, platform services, network health and liquidity connections are monitored continuously. Our engineers get alerted when something starts to look wrong, which usually means catching a problem before it reaches clients.

Security

Firewalls, tightly controlled admin access, secure connections for your team, regular patching and separation between servers. A trading server holds client data and controls real money, so we treat security as part of the build itself.

Backups

Automated backups on a schedule that suits your trading activity, stored away from your main server. We also restore from them on a regular basis to confirm they actually work.

Disaster Recovery

A written, practiced plan for what happens if your main server fails. Which server takes over, how data is restored, who does what and roughly how long each step takes. You'll have a copy, and so will we.

Performance Reviews

Every so often we look at how your environment is holding up. Resource trends, database growth, slow components, peak-time behaviour. That way upgrades happen when they're needed rather than after something breaks.

Technical Support

Our engineers stay responsible for your hosting after setup. Patching, capacity changes, alert response and help whenever your team needs it.

A Note on Forex VPS

You'll often see "forex VPS" advertised. In most cases that means a small virtual server a trader rents to run expert advisors around the clock. It's a useful product, but it's not the same as broker hosting.

What we provide is the infrastructure your brokerage runs on, meaning the servers behind your trading platform. That said, virtual servers can still be a perfectly good choice for parts of a broker's environment, especially for newer operations, and we'll recommend them where they make sense.

Home

How It Works

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

How Forex Brokerage Technology Setup Works

Building the technology behind a brokerage involves a lot of moving parts, and many founders start without a clear idea of what happens when. That uncertainty is usually where budgets stretch and deadlines slip.

The Four Stages at a Glance

01 Consultation → 02 Solution Design → 03 Integration → 04 Launch & Support

Each stage ends with something concrete you can review before we move forward. Nothing gets built on assumptions, and you won't be asked to approve work you haven't seen.

Stage 01: Consultation

This is where we get to know your business properly. It usually starts with a call, followed by a short questionnaire and, for larger projects, a few working sessions with your team.

What We Cover

* Your business model, whether that's a broker, a prop firm or a hybrid

* Target countries and the clients you expect to serve

* Execution approach and how you plan to handle order flow

* Platform preference, if you have one, or whether you'd like guidance

* Providers already signed or under discussion for liquidity, payments and verification

* Your timeline, including any regulatory milestones the launch depends on

* Budget range, so recommendations stay realistic

What You Get

A clear summary of your requirements, written back to you so we can both confirm we've understood the business correctly. If something you want isn't technically sensible, this is where we'll say so.

Stage 03: Integration

This is the build. Servers go up, platforms are configured and systems get connected to each other.

Infrastructure and Platform

Hosting environments are provisioned and secured. The trading platform is installed or set up under your chosen arrangement, with groups, symbols, account types and trading conditions configured to your specification.

Connectivity

Liquidity connections are established in a staging environment first, symbols are mapped and routing rules applied.

Operational Systems

Your CRM, verification provider, payment providers, website registration and any mobile app are connected to the platform and to each other.

Third-Party Coordination

Liquidity providers, payment companies and verification services each need credentials issued, test environments opened and sometimes certification completed. We handle the technical back-and-forth so you aren't stuck relaying messages between engineers.

Testing and Acceptance

Before anything goes live, we test the whole chain with realistic scenarios. Pricing accuracy, order execution, rejections, margin events, swaps, onboarding, deposits, withdrawals, partner commissions and reporting. Then your own team runs through their daily tasks in the test environment and signs off when satisfied. Anything that fails gets fixed and checked again.

What You Get

A fully working, tested environment and written confirmation of what was tested and passed.

Stage 04: Launch & Support

Go-Live

We agree on a launch date and time, usually a quieter market period. Production credentials are switched on, monitoring is active, and our engineers are watching closely as the first real clients arrive.

Early Stabilisation

The opening weeks often reveal small things no test could predict, like a payment method behaving oddly in one country or a symbol setting that needs adjusting once real volume appears. We stay close during this period and fix issues quickly.

Ongoing Support

After stabilisation, you move onto a support arrangement covering monitoring, maintenance, configuration changes, updates and help when your team needs it. As your business grows, we add providers, markets, features and capacity.

What You Get

A live brokerage, documentation describing your setup, and a team that already understands your environment when you need changes later.

DELIVERY PROCESS

Consultation

Integration

Launch support

Integrated technology workflow

What We'll Need From You

Projects run smoothly when a few things are in place on your side:

* A main contact who can make decisions or get them made quickly

* Signed agreements with liquidity, payment and verification providers, or progress toward them

* Branding assets such as logos, colours and fonts

* Your onboarding, withdrawal and risk policies, even in draft

* Time from your team for testing before launch

* Clarity on your regulatory position and any conditions attached to it

KYC & AML

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

KYC & AML Integration for Forex Brokers

Verification is the first real conversation a new client has with your brokerage. If it's clumsy, slow or confusing, a good number of people simply give up and go elsewhere. If it's too loose, you're exposed to fraud, bad actors and serious regulatory trouble.

Why Brokers Need This Done Properly

Most brokerages start out verifying clients by hand. A passport photo arrives by email, someone eyeballs it, a utility bill follows a day later, and approval gets noted in a spreadsheet. That's manageable at twenty sign-ups a week. At two hundred, it falls apart.

Manual handling also leaves gaps. Documents get lost in inboxes. Nobody's sure who approved which client. Expired IDs go unnoticed. And when a regulator or banking partner asks to see your onboarding records, pulling together a coherent answer takes days.

Integrated verification fixes the mechanics. Your compliance people still make the calls that need human judgement, but the collecting, checking, routing and record-keeping run on rails.

VERIFICATION WORKFLOW

Client documents

Verification

Review history

Integrated technology workflow

Who This Helps

* Brokers launching soon who want verification built in from the first client

* Firms whose compliance staff are drowning in manual document checks

* Brokerages expanding into countries with different ID types and onboarding rules

* Businesses that failed a banking or payment provider review over weak onboarding records

* Prop firms that need to verify traders before releasing funded accounts or payouts

How We Approach a Project

01 Consultation

We start with your compliance policy, target markets, current onboarding process and any providers you already use or are considering.

02 Solution Design

Together we define the verification flow for each client type, which checks happen where, how risk is assessed, who reviews what and what each status allows a client to do. You sign off on the design before we build.

03 Integration

Providers are connected, the workflow is configured in your CRM and onboarding screens, and status sync with your trading platform is set up. We test with sample identities, edge cases and failure scenarios, such as blurry uploads, mismatched names and provider timeouts.

04 Launch & Support

We go live and keep watch over the early volume, tuning the flow where clients stumble. After that, we handle changes as your policies, providers or markets evolve.

Where Verification Fits in the Client Journey

Registration → ID & Document Capture → Verification Provider Checks → Screening & Risk Rating → Compliance Review Queue → Approved / More Info Needed / Rejected → CRM Status Update → Deposits & MT4 / MT5 Account Access

A client signs up and is prompted to verify. Their documents go to your provider for automated checks, then through screening and risk rating. Clear cases can move quickly, while flagged ones wait for a reviewer. Whatever the decision, it updates the CRM and controls whether the client can fund and trade.

Benefits for Your Brokerage

Fewer Drop-Offs

A smooth, mobile-friendly verification step keeps more of the prospects your marketing has paid for.

A Lighter Compliance Workload

Automation takes the routine checks, so your team spends time on genuine edge cases instead of squinting at clear passport scans.

Records You Can Stand Behind

A complete, time-stamped onboarding history makes reviews by banks, payment partners and regulators far less stressful.

Consistency

Every client goes through the same defined steps for their profile. No more approvals depending on who happened to be on shift.

Easier Expansion

New countries and document types can be added to the flow without rebuilding your onboarding from scratch.

item.title: Forex Liquidity & Connectivity Solutions
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Home

Solutions

Liquidity & Connectivity

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Forex Liquidity & Connectivity Solutions

Every quote your clients see and every trade they place depends on one thing working quietly in the background: the line between your trading platform and the market. When that line is clean, nobody thinks about it. When it isn't, you hear about it within minutes.

What Is Forex Liquidity?

Put simply, liquidity is the availability of buyers and sellers ready to trade at a given price. For a brokerage, it usually arrives through a liquidity provider. That might be a bank, a prime broker, a prime-of-prime firm or a non-bank market maker, each streaming bid and ask prices and accepting orders against them.

Your clients never deal with those institutions directly. They trade on your platform. Your platform, in turn, needs a reliable technical route to the provider so prices come in accurately and orders go out quickly. That route is what we mean by connectivity, and it's where a surprising number of brokerage problems begin.

EXECUTION CONNECTIVITY

Trading platform

Bridge / FIX

Liquidity providers

Integrated technology workflow

Who Comes to Us for This

* Startups wiring up their very first provider ahead of launch

* Established brokers wanting a second source for depth or as a safety net

* Firms switching providers and needing zero downtime during the changeover

* Operations troubled by unexplained rejects, odd spreads or quotes that stop updating

* Prop trading businesses needing external pricing or hedging links

* Brokers ready to graduate from a single feed to a multi-provider pool

What We Deliver

Liquidity Provider Integration

Before touching any configuration, we gather your provider's technical documentation. Supported protocols, session schedules, instrument lists, minimum and maximum order sizes, permitted order types, and whatever conformance testing they insist on. We flag mismatches early, while they're still cheap to resolve.

Liquidity Bridge Setup

A bridge is middleware that sits between your server and one or more providers. It typically handles markups, routing logic, risk-based splitting of flow and multi-source pricing. We install it, configure it to your instructions and connect it at both ends. This is especially useful if you plan to grow beyond one provider.

MT5 Gateway Configuration

Where a provider offers a native MT5 gateway, it can be a lighter, more direct option with fewer moving pieces. Fine for straightforward setups with a single source and simple routing. We'll tell you honestly whether a gateway is enough or whether a bridge would serve you better.

FIX API Connectivity

FIX, short for Financial Information eXchange, is the protocol institutions use to swap price and order messages. Most bridges and many gateways speak FIX under the hood. We establish and certify these sessions, sort out network routing, credentials and heartbeats, and make sure reconnection behaves sensibly after a drop.

Liquidity Aggregation

With two or more providers, aggregation merges their price streams into a single book. Orders can then route by best price, by fixed allocation or by whatever logic you specify. It can tighten what clients see and spread your dependence. It also introduces extra settings to manage, which we'll explain upfront.

MT4 and MT5 Integration

Whichever platform you run, or both, we link it with your chosen connector, aligning account groups, execution modes and the way fills are reported back. Brokers running MT4 and MT5 in parallel can share a single bridge, so pricing stays consistent across the two.

Symbol Mapping

Providers and platforms rarely name or size instruments identically. One might list gold in ounces, another in lots of a hundred. Suffixes differ. Decimal places differ. Session hours differ. We line up every instrument manually and verify contract size, precision, trading hours and margin currency for each. Sloppy mapping is a classic source of costly mistakes, so this gets real attention.

Order Routing

You decide your execution model. Pass everything to the market, keep some flow internally, or use a hybrid split based on account group, trade size or client profile. We translate those decisions into working rules, test them and document them so your dealing team knows exactly what's configured.

Monitoring

After go-live, we track feed freshness, session status, fill rates, rejection counts and round-trip timing to each provider. Unusual patterns trigger alerts for our engineers, and you get a clear explanation of what happened if something needs investigating.

How We Run a Connectivity Project

01 Consultation

We talk through your providers, platform, execution model and what you expect from the setup. If you haven't picked a provider yet, we can outline the technical questions worth asking each candidate.

02 Solution Design

We decide between bridge, gateway or direct FIX, plan any aggregation and backup paths, and document how routing will work. You approve the design before build work begins.

03 Integration

Connections go up in a staging environment first. Symbols get mapped, routing gets configured, and we run thorough tests. Normal fills, partial fills, rejections, behaviour around rollover and weekend open, and what happens when a feed briefly disconnects. Any provider certification gets completed here too.

04 Launch & Support

We move to production at an agreed time, watch closely through the opening sessions and then shift to ongoing monitoring and maintenance.

The Connectivity Chain at a Glance

Client Terminal → MT4 / MT5 Server → Bridge or Gateway → FIX Session → Primary Provider

Bridge → Secondary Provider (Aggregation or Failover)

Fills & Confirmations → Server → Client Terminal & Back Office Reporting

Orders leave the platform, pass through your connector and reach a provider over FIX. Where a second provider is in place, the bridge can blend pricing from both or switch over if the first becomes unavailable. Every confirmation returns along the chain and lands in your reports, giving your dealing desk a full picture.

Home

Solutions

MT5 White Label

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

MT5 White Label Solutions for Forex Brokers

An MT5 white label lets you put your own brand on the MT5 trading platform without buying and running a full server licence yourself. Your clients see your name. You control your own trading groups, symbols and condition

What an MT5 White Label Actually Means

There's a fair bit of confusion around this term, so let's keep it simple.

MT5 runs on a server operated under a licence from the platform developer. With a full licence, you own and run that server yourself. That gives you the most control, but it also comes with a large upfront cost and a lot of technical responsibility.

With a white label, your brokerage operates within an existing licensed MT5 environment. You get your own branded setup, your own client groups and manager access to run your business day to day. The core server sits under the licence holder's arrangement rather than yours.

For most new brokers, that trade-off makes sense. Lower startup costs, faster time to market, and you can always look at moving to a full deployment later as volumes grow.

One important point. A white label is a technology arrangement. It isn't a financial licence and it doesn't give you permission to offer trading services anywhere. That part is covered further down.

YOUR BRANDED ENVIRONMENT

Branded terminals

MT5 groups

Liquidity link

Integrated technology workflow

Who It Suits

A white label MT5 setup tends to work well for:

* New brokers who want to launch on MT5 without committing to a full server licence on day one

* Introducing brokers ready to move clients under their own brand

* Regional brokerages testing a new market before investing in bigger infrastructure

* Businesses currently on MT4 who want to move to MT5 without a heavy upfront spend

If you already process high volumes, need deep control over server-level settings or plan to run several entities from one environment, a full deployment might suit you better. We're happy to talk through both.

How the Deployment Works

01 Requirements

We start with your business model. Which markets, which instruments, which account types, which liquidity provider. These answers shape every configuration decision that follows.

02 Environment Setup

Your white label environment is created and branded, with server access and hosting arranged.

03 Configuration

Groups, symbols, trading conditions and manager permissions get configured. This step takes care, because small mistakes here, like a wrong contract size or margin setting, can turn into real money problems later.

04 Connectivity and Integrations

Liquidity is connected, and your CRM, KYC and payment providers are linked to MT5.

05 Testing

We test pricing, execution, rejects, margin calls, stop outs, swaps and commissions, along with the full client journey from sign-up to first trade. Your team joins in to check its own workflows.

06 Launch and Ongoing Support

Go-live with monitoring in place. After that, we handle configuration changes, new symbols, new account types and day-to-day technical issues as your brokerage grows.

Where the White Label Sits in Your Stack

Client → Branded MT5 Terminals (Desktop, Web, Mobile) → Your MT5 Groups & Settings → Bridge / Gateway / FIX → Liquidity Provider

Client Portal & CRM ↔ MT5 Manager Access ↔ KYC & Payment Providers

Your clients only ever see your brand. Behind the terminals, their accounts sit in groups configured for your business. Orders route out to your liquidity provider, while your CRM keeps client records, verification status, deposits and trading accounts in sync with MT5.

Key Capabilities

* Branded MT5 access across desktop, web and mobile

* Multiple account types with separate leverage, commission and swap settings

* Symbol-level control over spreads, markups, sessions and margin

* Role-based manager access for dealing, risk and support teams

* Bridge, gateway or FIX liquidity connectivity

* Automated account creation from your CRM

* KYC and payment provider integration

* IB and partner group setup

* Ongoing configuration changes and technical support

* A clear path to a full MT5 deployment when you're ready

Home

Products

Payment Gateway

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Payment Gateway Integration for Forex Brokers

Money moving in and out is where client trust gets won or lost. A deposit that takes hours to show up in a trading account makes people nervous. A withdrawal stuck in limbo makes them angry. And a finance team reconciling payments line by line against bank statements is a finance team that never gets ahead.

Why Payments Are Harder for Brokers

Online shops take a payment and ship a product. Brokers deal with something messier. Money arrives in many currencies, through many methods, from clients in many countries. It has to land in the correct trading account, often within minutes. Then, unlike most businesses, you also have to send money back out, regularly and securely, after checking it's going to the right person.

On top of that, forex is treated as higher risk by many payment companies, so brokers often end up juggling several providers. Each one has its own API, its own status codes, its own settlement timing and its own quirks. Without proper integration, the result is manual work, delays and errors that are painful to unpick later.

PAYMENT OPERATIONS

Client portal

Provider status

Reconciliation

Integrated technology workflow

Who This Is For

* Brokers setting up their first payment methods ahead of launch

* Brokerages adding local payment options to grow in new regions

* Firms whose deposits still need someone to manually credit trading accounts

* Businesses that have lost a provider before and want backup routes in place

* Prop firms handling challenge fees on the way in and trader payouts on the way out

How a Payment Integration Project Runs

01 Consultation

We look at your target markets, preferred payment methods, existing provider agreements, withdrawal policy and current pain points.

02 Solution Design

We plan provider connections, deposit and withdrawal flows, approval rules, routing logic and reconciliation reporting. You approve the design before development starts.

03 Integration

Each provider is connected in its test environment first. We run through successful payments, declines, partial refunds, reversals, delayed confirmations and duplicate notifications. Withdrawal approvals and balance updates are tested end to end.

04 Launch & Support

We move to live credentials, monitor early transactions closely and stay on hand to add providers, adjust routing or resolve issues as your business grows.

How the Payment Flow Connects

Client Portal → Deposit Request → Payment Provider Secure Page → Provider Confirmation via Webhook → CRM Transaction Record → MT4 / MT5 Balance Update

Client Portal → Withdrawal Request → Finance Approval Queue → Payout via Provider → CRM Record → MT4 / MT5 Balance Update

All Transactions → Daily Reconciliation Report

Deposits flow from the portal through the provider and back as a confirmed transaction that credits the trading account. Withdrawals travel the other way, pausing for approval before payout. Every movement feeds the reconciliation report so nothing slips through unnoticed.

Benefits for Your Brokerage

Quicker Funding

Clients see deposits on their accounts soon after paying, which means they can start trading while they're still keen.

Controlled Payouts

Withdrawals follow your rules every time, with a clear record of who approved what.

Less Manual Finance Work

Automatic crediting and daily reconciliation free your finance team from the spreadsheet grind.

Resilience

Backup providers keep clients funding even when one provider has a bad day.

Room to Expand

Adding a local payment method for a new market becomes a manageable project, not a rebuild.

item.title: Prop Firm CRM API & Trading Technology
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Home

Products

Prop Firm Technology

FOREX TRADE TECHNOLOGY

Prop Firm CRM API & Trading Technology

Running a prop firm means watching thousands of evaluation accounts at once, each with its own target, drawdown limit and deadline. A trader breaches a rule at 3am and the account needs closing. Another passes and expects their funded account by morning. Someone requests a payout, and your team has to confirm the trading behind it was genuine.

What Makes Prop Firm Operations Different

A brokerage cares about deposits, trading activity and client retention. A prop firm's concerns sit somewhere else entirely. You're selling evaluations, measuring traders against strict rules, deciding who progresses, and paying out a share of profits to the ones who succeed.

Standard broker CRMs weren't built for that cycle. They don't know what a daily loss limit is, can't move a trader from phase one to phase two, and won't tell you that three accounts are copying each other's trades. Prop firms need tooling designed around evaluation logic, and that's what this is.

PROP TRADING OPERATIONS

Challenges

Rule monitoring

Progression

Integrated technology workflow

Who It's For

* New prop firms planning their first challenge programme

* Growing firms whose manual checks are starting to miss breaches or delay funded accounts

* Brokers adding a prop trading division alongside their regular business

* Firms moving to a new trading platform and needing their rules rebuilt properly

* Operators wanting to offer several challenge types, sizes and pricing tiers

What's Included

Challenge and Evaluation Setup

Single-phase, two-phase, instant funding or custom models. You define account sizes, profit targets, minimum trading days, time limits, leverage and pricing for each, and the system handles the rest.

Checkout and Account Creation

Traders choose a challenge on your website, pay through your integrated payment provider and receive their trading account automatically. No one on your team has to create logins manually.

Trader Accounts and Progression

Each trader's journey is tracked from purchase through each phase to funded status. Passing a phase can trigger the next account automatically or send it for review first, whichever your process requires.

Rule Configuration

Daily loss limits, maximum drawdown (static or trailing), profit targets, consistency rules, minimum days, news trading restrictions, weekend holding, lot size caps and more. Rules can differ between challenge types and phases.

Real-Time Rule Monitoring

The system checks trading activity against each account's rules as it happens. When a breach occurs, the account can be disabled automatically and the trader notified with the reason, so there's no argument about what happened or when.

Risk Monitoring

Dashboards flag patterns worth a closer look, such as identical trades across linked accounts, suspected copy trading, hedging between accounts, latency arbitrage behaviour or unusual concentration in a single instrument.

Performance Dashboards

Traders see their progress against targets and limits in a clear dashboard, which cuts down support questions. Your team sees firm-wide views of active challenges, pass rates, breach reasons and revenue.

Payout Review Workflow

Payout requests from funded traders arrive in a review queue with trading history, rule compliance and risk flags attached. Your team approves or queries each request, and approved payouts go out through your payment provider with a full record kept.

CRM and Admin Panel

Trader profiles, KYC status, purchase history, account history, support notes and communication logs in one place, with role-based access for support, risk and finance staff.

API Access

A documented API lets your website, affiliate system, payment providers, KYC service and trading platform exchange data with the CRM. Useful if you want a custom front end or need to plug in tools you already use.

How Everything Connects

Trader → Your Website & Checkout → Payment Provider → Prop Firm CRM → Automatic Account Creation on Trading Platform

Trading Platform → Live Trading Data → Rule Engine & Risk Monitoring → Breach / Pass / Progression Actions

Funded Trader → Payout Request → Review Queue → Payment Provider → Record in CRM

A trader buys a challenge on your site, pays and gets an account straight away. As they trade, data streams back to the rule engine, which enforces limits and moves accounts between phases. Funded traders request payouts, your team reviews them, and approved payments go out with everything logged.

Benefits for Your Firm

Consistent Rule Enforcement

Every trader is measured the same way, every time, with timestamps to back it up.

Faster Progression

Traders who pass move forward quickly, which keeps them happy and talking positively about your firm.

Earlier Warning on Abuse

Risk flags surface suspicious behaviour before it turns into a costly payout.

A Smaller Support Load

Clear dashboards and automatic notifications answer most of the questions traders would otherwise email about.

Ready to Scale

Whether you run five hundred accounts or fifty thousand, the same automation handles the volume without hiring an army.
